Manager Dave Roberts made the change due to Ohtani's struggles at the plate following injuries that caused him to miss time toward the end of the regular season. item.title: Astronomers Identify Potential Candidate for Planet Nine in Infrared Surveys
item.description: Astronomers have identified a faint infrared object that may represent the first direct evidence of Planet Nine, a hypothetical planet believed to exist beyond Neptune. The discovery comes from analyzing decades-old infrared observations, specifically comparing data from the Infrared Astronomical Satellite (IRAS) in 1983 and Japan's AKARI spacecraft in 2006-2007. Researchers found a single object that appeared to move across the sky between the two surveys, with a shift of 47.46 arcminutes—approximately one and a half times the apparent width of the full Moon. This movement aligns with what would be expected from a large planet located hundreds of astronomical units from the Sun, roughly 500-700 AU away, with a mass between 7 and 17 times that of Earth. The object's brightness and slow motion match theoretical predictions for Planet Nine, though the researchers emphasize this is not definitive proof. item.title: Strategists Still Expect U.S. Treasury Yields to Decline Despite Recent Surge
item.description:
Fixed-income strategists continue to expect U.S. Treasury yields to decline over the coming months, even after the benchmark 10-year yield recorded its largest quarterly increase since 1994. A Reuters poll of nearly 60 strategists conducted from October 5 to 7 found median forecasts for the 10-year yield to fall to 5.00% by the end of the year, 4.90% in six months, and 4.75% in one year.
However, confidence in that outlook has weakened. Strategists have underestimated the 10-year yield in nine consecutive monthly surveys this year and incorrectly predicted its direction in six of the past nine months. The yield has risen nearly 120 basis points this year and recently reached 5.34%, its highest level since 2002.

item.description:

The OpenAI Decisions API is designed to provide direct answers to bounded questions from a fixed list of options, without generating additional text or inventing new options. This approach eliminates the need for parsing generated text and ensures the response is always one of the provided choices.
The author demonstrates two primary methods for integrating the Decisions API with Strands Agents. The first method involves selecting the appropriate tool before the model runs, which reduces token usage and improves accuracy. By using the Decisions API to choose from a predefined list of tools, the agent avoids the pitfalls of a small model having to select from a large pool of overlapping tools. item.description: Senator Thom Tillis (R-NC) strongly defended Senator Mitch McConnell (R-KY) against questions about McConnell's health and ability to serve out his term, during an appearance on MS NOW to promote his book 'How to Lose Friends and Antagonize Presidents.' The North Carolina Republican bristled when host Peter Alexander suggested that McConnell should step down due to his age and health issues, comparing the situation to President Joe Biden's debate performance. item.description: The newly unveiled photo strip captures country music icon Dolly Parton and her late husband Carl Dean in a playful, candid moment during their early relationship in the 1960s. Dolly Parton herself had not seen the photos since they were taken, and the discovery left her 'floored' when the images were uncovered by archivists. The museum exhibit provides a rare glimpse into the private, lighthearted side of the couple's relationship before Dolly's rise to global stardom. item.description: A retired Special Forces officer, Mike Nelson, has warned that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth could be removed from his position following the 2026 midterm elections if President Donald Trump seeks to blame someone for the unpopularity of the ongoing war with Iran. Nelson, a former Army officer with over two decades of service and now a fellow at the National Security Institute, made these remarks on a podcast hosted by New York Times columnist David French. Nelson emphasized that the current conflict with Iran is 'the least popular war since World War II, since modern polling,' suggesting that the administration may face mounting pressure to find a scapegoat. item.description: Attorney General Todd Blanche expressed frustration over a significant number of prosecutors leaving the Justice Department, stating that those who departed 'hate us' and have formed an organization to oppose the department under President Donald Trump's leadership. In an interview on the Ruthless podcast, Blanche acknowledged that while most department employees are 'great,' changing the 'perception of the culture' has been his most challenging task. He specifically referenced over 5,000 employees who resigned, retired, or were fired during Trump's first year in office, including 14 attorneys in Minnesota who left the U.S. Attorney's Office in a single month due to directives related to an immigration crackdown. item.title: Trump Advisers Travel to Balkans for Pro-Russia Election Advisory Amid U.S. Midterm Campaign
item.description: Republican operatives are expressing anger and frustration after discovering that two of President Donald Trump's top political advisers, James Blair and Chris LaCivita, traveled to Republika Srpska, a self-governing territory in Bosnia and Herzegovina, to advise a pro-Russia government ahead of its elections. The New York Times reported that Blair and LaCivita, who manage Trump's political operation's midterm ad campaign, were paid hundreds of thousands of dollars by a Washington law firm hired by the territory's government for counsel on voting issues. The trip has sparked criticism within the GOP, with one operative stating, 'We are out here fighting for our lives and these dudes are in some random a-- country made up of too many consonants no one has ever heard of taking hundreds of thousands of dollars while telling all of us to chill out because they've got it.' item.title: NVIDIA cuPhoton Accelerates Scientific Image Processing for Astronomy and Beyond
item.description: NVIDIA cuPhoton is a new toolkit designed to accelerate scientific image analysis, particularly for astronomy and other fields requiring high-performance computing. The technical blog post details how cuPhoton leverages GPU acceleration to process astronomical images efficiently, focusing on two key tasks: image subtraction and dipole fitting for moving objects like asteroids. The toolkit uses a Gaussian-polynomial kernel basis for optimal image subtraction, ensuring flux conservation and compact kernel representation. For dipole fitting, cuPhoton employs a GaussianDipoleModel to identify moving objects through paired positive and negative flux regions in difference images. The blog demonstrates a synthetic example with a planted mover (simulated asteroid) to validate the workflow, showing how the toolkit can accurately recover the positions of moving objects. item.description: California Democrats, led by Senators Adam Schiff and Alex Padilla and Representative Salud Carbajal, have sent a letter to Brittany Kelm, a former White House energy adviser, demanding answers regarding her transition to a position at Sable Offshore Corp., an oil company she had previously assisted while in government. Kelm served as a senior adviser on the National Energy Dominance Council, where part of her responsibilities included aiding Sable Offshore Corp. in restarting oil production from platforms off Santa Barbara. Her departure from the White House in August to join Sable as vice president of policy and commercial has raised ethical concerns, particularly as California officials have long opposed Sable's operations due to an oil spill in the area. item.description: In a significant development for Merck & Co., a Dutch court has ruled that the pharmaceutical company infringed on a patent held by Halozyme Therapeutics related to a subcutaneous formulation of its blockbuster cancer drug Keytruda. The court order mandates Merck to cease manufacturing and marketing the subcutaneous version of Keytruda in several European markets, including France, Italy, Sweden, Switzerland, and the Netherlands. This ruling represents a setback for Merck in its ongoing patent dispute with Halozyme, which has been expanding in scope. The existing intravenous formulation of Keytruda remains unaffected by this legal action, ensuring continued patient access to the standard treatment. Keytruda, a leading immunotherapy for various cancers, has been a major revenue driver for Merck, generating billions annually. item.description: Michigan Republican Senate nominee Mike Rogers is distancing himself from President Donald Trump's trade policies, particularly the 50 percent tariffs imposed on Canadian imports, in a new campaign ad. The ad, set in a bar, emphasizes Michigan's cultural ties to Canada, featuring a reference to drinking Labatt beer and watching the Detroit Red Wings. Rogers states, 'Here in Michigan, we know that Canada is not our enemy. We need to end this tariff war — now. As Michigan's senator, I'll bring both parties together to lower your prices. item.title: UK Financial Watchdog to Review Handling of Whistleblower Who Exposed Lutnick-Epstein Ties
item.description: A formal review has been launched into the British Financial Conduct Authority's (FCA) handling of Simon Andriesz, a whistleblower who exposed Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's business ties to Jeffrey Epstein, following the banker's suicide. Andriesz, 57, died by suicide on September 23 in Thailand, according to his family. He had been a former managing director at Lutnick's brokerage BGC and spent over a decade accusing the firm of misconduct, winning $500,000 in a 2024 arbitration against BGC. His disclosures contributed to a $3 million federal penalty against BGC in 2019. Andriesz also informed the FBI in 2020 and 2021 about Lutnick's undisclosed business ties to Epstein, citing 2018 emails about a shared stake in an advertising startup called Adfin. item.description: Queen Camilla has paid tribute to Jeffrey Archer, the bestselling author and former Conservative politician who died at age 86. In a statement, the Queen described Archer as 'an exception to the end' and noted that he lived a life 'as rich, varied and colourful as any of the characters in their books, or with as many surprising plot twists.' She acknowledged that Archer was 'not without flaw,' but emphasized that friends would remember him as an 'irrepressible life force' throughout his many life chapters. Archer, known for his 300 million book sales and novels like the Clifton Chronicles and Kane and Abel, had a tumultuous career that included a 2001 perjury conviction related to a libel case against the Daily Star. item.description: The Republican Party is facing growing internal concerns that the 'industrial-strength MAGA racism' they have promoted may backfire in Ohio's gubernatorial race. item.description: Internal emails obtained by The Washington Post reveal that the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), under pressure from the Trump White House, significantly reduced training requirements for outside law enforcement agencies participating in immigration enforcement operations. The training period for officers from partner departments was cut from four weeks of in-person instruction to just 40 hours of virtual training. item.description: The European Commission is reportedly exploring a new tax approach targeting large corporations operating within the European Union, aiming to generate revenue without singling out specific American tech giants. According to a Financial Times report, the EU is considering expanding its 'Corporate Resource for Europe' (CORE) proposal to require all companies with over €100 million in annual revenue to pay an annual lump-sum tax contribution. This would replace the current CORE system, which imposes fixed annual levies between €100,000 and €750,000 on qualifying firms, capturing only a small portion of multinational earnings. James Talarico has become a focal point for Trump's political influence, with sources indicating that a Paxton loss would represent a significant setback for the former president's endorsement credibility. item.description:
Royal Mail has announced plans to cut up to 2,500 jobs in its head office and support functions by the end of 2027 as part of a major organizational restructuring. The cuts, which represent less than 2% of the company's total workforce of approximately 131,000 employees, will not affect frontline postal workers such as posties and drivers. Instead, the reductions will focus on administrative and support roles through voluntary redundancies and natural attrition as employees leave the organization.
The decision comes as Royal Mail faces significant challenges from a dramatic decline in letter delivery volumes, which have dropped more than 70% since their peak in the mid-2000s. item.description: Senate Republican leaders are preparing for the possibility of a sudden Supreme Court vacancy, particularly as they face the risk of losing their majority in the upcoming 2026 midterm elections. According to a Politico report, a Democratic victory would have significant implications for Donald Trump's presidency, potentially leading to the Senate blocking confirmations of his judicial nominees. The article describes this scenario as a 'nightmare' for Republicans, who have long viewed their reshaping of the federal judiciary as a key achievement of Trump's legacy. She gained recognition through her roles in Czech films such as 'Lemonade Joe' (1964) and 'Who Wants to Kill Jessie?', later expanding her career to include German, Italian, and English-language productions like 'The Vengeance of She' (1968). Known for her blonde beauty and natural screen presence, Schoberová became the first Czech woman to appear on the cover of Playboy. After marrying Hollywood producer John Calley in the early 1970s, she largely retired from acting, leaving behind a brief but impactful career that captured the essence of the 1960s era. Her work remains a significant part of cinematic history, reflecting the cultural and artistic vibrancy of the decade. OpenAI has announced the release of solutions to 377 open mathematical problems, marking another major milestone in the application of artificial intelligence to advanced research. The results, produced by an internal, unreleased frontier AI model, span multiple subdisciplines including algebra, number theory, topology, mathematical logic, and theoretical computer science. According to OpenAI, each solution required an average of about three hours of compute time equivalent to ChatGPT Pro usage, and many of the proofs have already been formally verified using Lean, a programming language that checks the logical validity of mathematical arguments.

item.title: Eva Marie Saint, Iconic Hollywood Star of Golden Age, Dies at 102
item.description: Legendary actress Eva Marie Saint, considered the last major surviving star of Hollywood's Golden Age, has died at the age of 102. She passed away from natural causes on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, at her home in Los Angeles, surrounded by her family. Saint's career spanned over seven decades across film, stage, and television, with her most notable roles including Edie Doyle in 'On the Waterfront' (1954), for which she won an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress, and Eve Kendall in 'North by Northwest' (1959) opposite Cary Grant. She also starred in 'Exodus' (1960), 'The Sandpiper' (1965), and 'Grand Prix' (1966), and later appeared in 'Superman Returns' (2005) as Martha Kent. Saint was nominated for five Emmys throughout her career, winning a Primetime Emmy in 1990 for 'People Like Us.' item.title: Study Challenges Assumption That Everyday Aggression Leads to Lethal Violence in Primates
item.description: A groundbreaking study from the University of Lincoln, UK, published in the journal Evolution Letters, challenges the long-held belief that everyday aggression in primates, including humans, inevitably escalates to lethal violence. The research analyzed patterns of aggression across 100 primate species, revealing that mild conflicts and lethal attacks follow distinct evolutionary pathways rather than forming a single behavioral spectrum. The findings indicate that species exhibiting frequent mild aggression are not necessarily more prone to lethal violence, and that extreme behaviors such as infanticide and killing adult rivals appear to evolve through separate mechanisms. Professor Bonaventura Majolo, lead author of the study, emphasized that this distinction adds complexity to the debate about whether violence is an inherent part of human nature. item.title: Portrait Artist Jonathan Yeo Reflects on Identity, Perception, and the Power of Being Seen
item.description: British portrait artist Jonathan Yeo discusses the difficulty of capturing a person’s true appearance and inner character in portraiture. In remarks connected with Sky Arts’ Artist of the Year, Yeo suggests that people rarely have an objective sense of how they look, because self-image is shaped by memory, habit, emotion, and the way others respond to us. His observation frames portraiture as more than a technical exercise in reproducing facial features: it is an attempt to recognize the life, personality, and humanity of the person sitting for the artist. Yeo is widely known for portraits of prominent public figures, including King Charles III, whose first official painted portrait after the coronation he created. His work has also included figures such as Sir David Attenborough, Malala Yousafzai, Idris Elba, and former British prime ministers. The article’s central idea is that a successful portrait can offer a subject a version of themselves that feels both unfamiliar and revealing.

item.description: The Iowa gubernatorial debate at St. Ambrose University on Tuesday descended into chaos as Republican candidate Zach Lahn repeatedly interrupted moderators and refused to stay on topic during a segment focused on agriculture policy. item.description:
President Donald Trump made a statement regarding his economic policies during a press briefing outside the White House on October 6, 2026, claiming that his administration had produced a 'strong dollar.' However, his remarks were met with immediate criticism from experts and commentators who pointed out the inaccuracy of his claim. Trump's interpretation of a 'strong dollar' was inconsistent with the standard economic understanding, where a strong dollar typically makes imports cheaper and exports more expensive. Instead, Trump seemed to conflate the concept with the absence of inflation, stating that a strong dollar 'gives you no inflation.'
This claim directly contradicted recent economic data released by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, which showed that inflation had risen to 3.4% in August 2026, driven largely by increased gasoline prices. item.description: Laos police have seized 521 kilograms of methamphetamine from a private jet that arrived at Luang Prabang International Airport from Malaysia. item.title: Understanding Indirect Prompt Injection in AI Agents: Risks and Defensive Strategies
item.description: The article discusses a security vulnerability in AI agents known as indirect prompt injection, which occurs when untrusted metadata or tool output is interpreted as instructions by the agent. Unlike direct prompt injection where malicious instructions are explicitly entered by a user, indirect injection happens when an attacker manipulates tool descriptions or the content returned by tools (such as web pages, emails, or database entries) to embed instructions that the agent follows without the user's knowledge. The article explains that current language models lack a hard boundary between control instructions and data, making them vulnerable to such attacks. The author outlines six defensive patterns to mitigate this risk: treating all tool output as untrusted data, vetting and pinning tool descriptions, enforcing allowlists for destinations and tools, applying least privilege to tool sets, gating side effects, and keeping humans involved in irreversible actions. item.description: The U.S. trade deficit reached its highest level in 17 months in August, marking a significant setback for President Donald Trump's tariff strategy aimed at reducing the gap. item.description: Senator Ted Cruz (R-TX), Chairman of the U.S. Senate Commerce Committee, has become a key supporter of Attorney General Ken Paxton's Senate campaign, positioning himself as a bridge between established Republican donors and the MAGA base. Cruz has acted as a part-time adviser and bundler for Paxton, who is trailing Democrat James Talarico in polls for the seat left vacant by retiring Senator John Cornyn. item.description: President Donald Trump has publicly criticized the New York Times for what he claims is a doctored photograph of his Miami golf resort, Trump National Doral Miami, in a series of posts on Truth Social late Monday night. item.description: The San Francisco 49ers secured a 24-14 victory over the Denver Broncos on Sunday, extending their undefeated record to 4-0. Head coach Kyle Shanahan achieved a milestone in the game, surpassing Bill Walsh for the most games coached in franchise history and securing his 95th win in that role. item.description: On October 5, 2026, former President Donald Trump made several verbal errors during a campaign rally in Grand Island, Nebraska, where he was supporting Republican candidates Governor Jim Pillen and Senator Pete Ricketts. The event took place on the first day of early voting in Nebraska, marking Trump's first campaign stop in the state since 2022. Trump initially stated, 'Probably, and I've known some bad governors, probably the worst governor in history, Jim Walz,' before correcting himself to say Minnesota Governor Tim Walz 'is, is the worst.' item.description: The Mashable team has provided comprehensive hints and answers for the New York Times Strands puzzle dated October 4, 2026. Strands is a word-search game that requires players to find words formed by connected letters in various directions—up, down, left, right, or diagonal—while allowing words to change direction, creating unique patterns. item.title: Astronomers Identify Elias 2-24b, Youngest Exoplanet Ever Observed, Challenging Formation Theories
item.description: Astronomers have confirmed the discovery of Elias 2-24b, the youngest exoplanet ever observed, estimated to be under 1 million years old. This discovery, led by a research team from Diego Portales University in Chile, challenges existing theories about planetary formation. The exoplanet orbits its star at approximately 55 astronomical units, a distance much farther than Jupiter's orbit around our sun, yet it has already formed into a gas giant within a remarkably short timeframe. The research team identified the planet by analyzing gaps in the protoplanetary disk surrounding the star Elias 2-24, using data from the W.M. Keck Observatory in Hawaii. They compared the position of a bright spot within a gap in the disk over time, confirming it was a planet gravitationally bound to the star rather than a background star or observational artifact. item.description: The article discusses the mounting legal and ethical challenges facing Todd Blanche, the former U.S. Attorney General under the Trump administration. item.description: The article explores the distinctive style of Vogue studio photography from the late 1940s to early 1950s, highlighting how photographers created polished images that emphasized silhouette, dramatic lighting, and the luxurious details of haute couture. item.description: Jim Bakker, a televangelist who co-founded the multimillion-dollar PTL (Promise Keepers, Television, and Life) ministry with his wife Tammy Faye, has died at the age of 86. Bakker and his wife were prominent figures in the televangelism industry during the 1980s, leading a religious empire that included a television network, a theme park, and various other ventures. However, their rise to fame was followed by a dramatic fall due to a series of scandals involving sexual misconduct and financial fraud. Bakker was convicted of fraud and conspiracy in the late 1980s, leading to his imprisonment. The scandal, which became one of the most infamous in American religious history, tarnished the Bakkers' reputation and led to the collapse of their PTL empire. Bakker's death on October 5, 2026, marks the end of a controversial career that spanned several decades. item.description: Sweden's national football team secured a 1-0 victory against Romania in a Nations League match held in Romania. The decisive goal was scored by Viktor Gyökeres in the 13th minute, which proved to be the difference in the match. The Swedes took an early lead when Alexander Bernhardsson delivered a cross towards Sebastian Nanasi, whose touch redirected the ball towards the post. Gyökeres capitalized on the opportunity to score the opening goal. Despite Romania's efforts to equalize, particularly in the second half with 53% possession and 13 shots (four on target), they were unable to find the back of the net. The match saw Sweden extend their unbeaten Nations League streak to 11 matches, with a chance to double their lead late in the game, though the ball hit the post. item.description:
New York has declared a state disaster emergency as measles cases continue to climb across the state. More than 100 cases have been reported this year, prompting Governor Kathy Hochul to take action to contain the outbreak. The emergency order, effective until at least November 4, expands the pool of health professionals who can administer the MMR (measles, mumps, and rubella) vaccine and order testing to include paramedics, pharmacists, midwives, and nurses.
State health officials are working closely with local departments to track and contain the spread of the highly contagious disease. Health Commissioner Dr. James McDonald emphasized that the MMR vaccine remains the best protection against measles and urged residents to verify their vaccination status.

item.description: Avery Norman's photographic series 'Cry to the Angels' has been recognized as one of five shortlisted projects for the LensCulture Photobook Prize 2026. Norman's images are entirely staged, reflecting her interest in photography's relationship with perception and truth. item.description: Imposiball is a new personal series by 3D artist Crtomir Just, featuring five short animations that play with the perception of shadows in sports settings. The series includes basketball, tennis, golf, swimming, and table tennis, each presented from a consistent isometric camera angle that flattens the court or field into a diagram-like view. Just uses flat slabs of color (such as clay orange, pool-tile blue, and mint green) and hard noon shadows to create minimalist scenes. The key element in each animation is that the shadows behave in ways that contradict the physical reality of the objects, creating a subtle but striking illusion. For example, in the table tennis animation, the paddle's shadow remains stationary while the paddle itself changes color, and the ball's shadow moves independently. item.title: NYPD Detective Released from Hospital Following Bronx Robbery Attack
item.description: A New York City Police Department (NYPD) detective, Jose Mercedes, has been released from Jacobi Medical Center after being stabbed multiple times during a robbery attempt in the Bronx. The incident occurred on Friday afternoon when Mercedes, who was off-duty, was clearing out the trunk of his car in the Norwood neighborhood. Two suspects on an e-bike attempted to snatch his gold chain, leading to a confrontation. Mercedes fought back, but was stabbed and slashed seven times before the attackers fled. item.title: Thoracic Ewing Sarcoma Presenting With Spinal Cord Compression in a Young Adult
item.description:
A case report describes a rare instance of thoracic Ewing sarcoma presenting as acute spinal cord compression in a 20-year-old man with no significant medical history. The patient experienced 10 days of heaviness in both lower limbs and urinary incontinence. Examination revealed flaccid paraplegia with complete motor loss, a sensory level at the T10 dermatome, and a left paravertebral mass.
Magnetic resonance imaging showed an extensive lesion involving the D10–D12 region of the thoracic spine. The mass extended into the spinal canal and left paravertebral soft tissues, producing significant spinal cord compression. The imaging findings were nonspecific, and a thoracoabdominal-pelvic CT scan found no other primary or metastatic sites. The patient underwent D10–D12 laminectomy and wide excision of the intraspinal and paravertebral components. His postoperative recovery was uncomplicated, and he experienced partial improvement in motor function.

item.description:
The United States urgently withdrew all 12 of its B-1 Air Force bombers from RAF Fairford, a military air base in southern England, following intelligence about a potential drone attack allegedly ordered by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. item.title: Alejandro G. Iñárritu Defends His Polarizing Climate Satire 'Digger'
item.description: Alejandro G. Iñárritu says the strong reactions to his new film, 'Digger,' are intentional. The Mexican filmmaker described the movie as a provocative satire about climate change, corporate power, and propaganda, with Tom Cruise playing an exaggerated oil magnate. Rather than offering clear answers, the film uses a bold conceptual style and a narrative twist designed to blur the boundary between truth and reality. Iñárritu argued that contemporary culture often prioritizes attention, likes, discomfort, and provocation, and that the film reflects that environment. Although critics have largely responded negatively and the movie's opening box-office performance has been weak, Iñárritu said he prefers a polarized response to indifference. He explained that he first conceived the idea while making his Oscar-winning drama 'The Revenant' in 2015. item.title: Elon Musk's Former Partners Provide Critical Insights in New Documentary on His Personal and Professional Life
item.description: The article discusses a new documentary titled 'Musk,' directed by Alex Gibney, which is set to premiere in theaters on October 16 and screen at the WIRED World Fair in Miami. The film, nearly four hours long, explores Elon Musk's rise as a tech mogul and his controversial personal life, with significant focus on his relationships with former partners Justine Wilson and Ashley St. Clair. Wilson, Musk's ex-wife, shares poignant details about the loss of their firstborn child to SIDS, which contrasts with Musk's public comments on the matter. She also recounts his derogatory remarks about their transgender daughter, Vivian Jenna Wilson, whom Musk claimed was 'killed by the woke mind virus.' Wilson describes Musk's behavior as gaslighting, stating he often criticized her and even said, 'If you were my employee, I would fire you.' item.description: The latest insider leaks regarding Ubisoft's upcoming Assassin's Creed Hexe have revealed significant details about the game's protagonist, supporting characters, and narrative setting. Set in 16th-century Germany during the witch trials, the game follows Anika Adler (referred to as 'Petra' in casting documents), a young woman accused of witchcraft who must navigate a dangerous historical period. The leaked character descriptions include her parents, Brigitte (a compassionate midwife) and Konrad (the headsman of Neustadt), as well as supporting characters like Bruno, Anton, and the mentor figure Wolfgang. The story also involves Mother Gertrud, a former healer turned outcast who offers refuge to the protagonist. The game is reportedly moving away from the RPG-heavy approach of recent Assassin's Creed titles toward a more linear, traditional experience. item.title: Trump Approves Firing Squad Execution for Fort Hood Shooter Nidal Hasan
item.description: President Donald Trump has approved the execution by firing squad of Army Maj. Nidal Malik Hasan for the 2009 shooting rampage at Fort Hood, Texas. The U.S. military has not carried out the death penalty since 1961. Hasan, an Army psychiatrist, opened fire at a medical building where soldiers were receiving checkups, shouting 'Allahu akbar' and killing 13 people while injuring over 30. He claimed his actions were to prevent soldiers from going to Afghanistan and killing his fellow Muslims, and made no effort to defend himself at trial. The Army secretary will determine the time and place for the execution, with Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell stating 'Judgement day for Hasan has finally come.' Hasan is one of four men currently on military death row at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas. The last military execution was in 1961, when Pvt. John Bennett was hanged for raping an 11-year-old girl. item.description: The NFL Players Association (NFLPA) has issued a statement condemning the comments made by line judge Jeff Seeman to Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride during a recent game between the Cardinals and the New York Giants. The incident occurred during Sunday's matchup, as captured by a CBS camera, showing Seeman interacting with McBride. While the exact words were not audible, the lip-reading community speculated that Seeman may have said something inappropriate, such as 'Thank you' twice, which raised concerns about the conduct of officials towards players. NFLPA executive director JC Tretter addressed the issue in a statement provided to Football Night in America before posting it on social media. Tretter emphasized that such behavior from officials towards players is unacceptable, noting that players are often held to higher standards when the roles are reversed. item.description: Dr. Mehmet Oz, the U.S. Center for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator under the Trump administration, faced skepticism on Fox News when he claimed that butter in America costs about $1 per stick. During a segment on Fox News, Oz stated, 'We went grocery shopping. Stick of butter, bag of peanuts. Butter in America is about a buck for a stick like this.' Fox News host Laura Ingraham immediately questioned him, asking, 'Where are you shopping?' and stating that butter does not cost $1 per stick in most places. Oz defended his claim, saying he had recently purchased butter for close to that price, though he acknowledged it might be 'going bad.' The article notes that while it is possible to find butter for around $1 per stick in certain regions, it is not the norm across the country. item.title: France to Close Up to 500 Schools Amid Escalating Student Protests Over Education Concerns
item.description: France is planning to fully or partially close up to 500 schools on Monday due to escalating student protests that have become increasingly violent. Education Minister Edouard Geffray announced the precautionary measures on Sunday, citing safety concerns as the security conditions have not been met. The closures are part of a bid for a 'partial, progressive return to lessons' following a weekend lull in protests. However, protest organizers have called for a resumption of large-scale demonstrations on Tuesday, arguing that the government has not taken 'concrete measures' to address their grievances. The protests, which began on September 17 in a Paris suburb over issues such as insufficient teaching staff, excessive school-day hours, and other complaints, have spread nationwide. Over 400 of France's 3,700 high schools were closed on Friday, with 560 facing protests or disruptions. item.title: Bronzeville Legacy Collective Raises $75 Million for Cultural Revitalization in Chicago's Historic Black Metropolis
item.description: The Bronzeville Legacy Collective, a network of eight community leaders in Chicago's Bronzeville neighborhood, has raised $75 million to build or redevelop nine cultural sites within the federally designated Bronzeville Black Metropolis National Heritage Area. The initiative aims to transform Bronzeville into a national destination for arts and culture, with projects including the National Museum of Gospel Music, the Emmett Till and Mamie Till-Mobley House, a food hub called Bronzeville Cookin', the Muddy Waters Mojo Museum, the Deeply Rooted Center for Black Dance and Creative Communities, Definition Theatre, The Forum arts and culture complex, and the South Side Community Art Center. The collective has a long-term goal of raising $250 million, including $100 million for the Bronzeville Trail, which will connect 40th and Federal streets to 41st Street and Lake Park Avenue by 2034. item.description: President Donald Trump was observed fixating on the legs of his senior aide Natalie Harp during a campaign rally in Grand Island, Nebraska, for Senator Pete Ricketts. The incident, which occurred shortly after Trump praised Harp as 'the perfect person,' drew immediate backlash from social media users and political commentators. item.title: Federal Judge Halts Trump Administration's $36 Billion Civil Fine Program Against Immigrants
item.description: A federal judge has issued a significant ruling against the Trump administration's civil fine program targeting immigrants, freezing a $36 billion 'punitive' fine machine. U.S. District Judge George O'Toole Jr., appointed by former President Bill Clinton, granted a stay against a June 2025 rule that allowed the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to issue massive fines without individual review. The rule, which permitted DHS to impose penalties for failing to leave the country, has reportedly resulted in over 65,000 fines totaling approximately $36 billion. The judge found that the administration violated legal standards by assuming willful noncompliance simply based on an individual's continued presence in the U.S. after a removal order, shifting the burden of proof to the recipient to prove they did not willfully violate the order. item.title: Trump Questions Red-Dye Diesel Policy After Signing Executive Order at Nebraska Rally
item.description: On October 5, 2026, during a campaign rally in Grand Island, Nebraska, President Donald Trump announced a new initiative regarding red-dye diesel, a type of fuel marked with a dye to indicate whether highway taxes have been paid. The president appeared confused about the policy he was signing, asking the crowd for clarification on what red-dye diesel was. Trump stated, 'Today, I am announcing another unprecedented step to bring down costs,' before questioning the audience about the fuel. He admitted, 'I don't know what the hell that is,' and asked, 'Does anyone want to explain it?' The crowd cheered, and Trump suggested that those in attendance understood the policy, saying, 'These guys, they know.' He then signed the executive order, which would allow anyone to purchase red-dye diesel for any purpose, and paraded his signature around the stage before handing his pen to a member of the crowd. item.title: 1887 Family Life in Buffalo, New York: A Glimpse into Domestic Scenes from the Late 19th Century
item.description: The article presents a collection of 35 historical photographs capturing family life near Buffalo, New York, in 1887. These images offer an intimate look at domestic scenes, small-town streets, and everyday moments shared by families in the surrounding area during the late 19th century. Rather than focusing on the bustling city center, the photographs highlight quiet, ordinary moments that reflect the slower pace and close-knit community atmosphere of the time. The collection includes posed group portraits, children playing, and simple outdoor settings, preserving a rare visual record of ordinary people and their world nearly 140 years ago. The photographs serve as a valuable historical resource, providing insight into the daily lives of families in the Buffalo area during a period of significant social and technological change. item.description: President Donald Trump has reversed his decision to fund nationwide political advertisements through taxpayer money, opting instead to finance them through his super PAC, MAGA, Inc. The announcement came after significant criticism from both Democrats and Republicans regarding the use of Customs and Border Protection funds for a controversial ad campaign that declared America 'will never be a communist country.' Trump initially defended the ads as a standard practice, stating they were a positive promotion for the United States. However, following reports that over $5.6 million in taxpayer funds had already been allocated to the campaign, Trump announced on his Truth Social platform that he would now fund the ads through his own political organization. item.description: U.S. District Judge Gary R. Brown has uncovered an elaborate hoax involving Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents who provided false testimony and falsified official records to conceal the illegal arrest of a Bronx man, Angel Jesus Almonte. The judge's ruling, issued on October 5, 2026, found that ICE agents arrested Almonte during a May 6 operation, mistakenly identifying him as a target for deportation. However, records revealed that the actual target was significantly different in physical appearance, being five inches shorter and 80 pounds lighter than Almonte. The agents claimed they mistook Almonte for the target, but the judge noted the discrepancy was obvious. During a bail hearing in June, three officers testified about witnessing drug deals involving Almonte, but one officer admitted he did not actually see anything in Almonte's hand. item.title: SpaceX Crew-13 Successfully Launches and Docks with ISS
item.description: The SpaceX Crew-13 mission successfully launched and docked with the International Space Station (ISS) on October 31, 2021. The mission, which carried four astronauts, marked a significant milestone in the ongoing collaboration between SpaceX and NASA. The crew, consisting of NASA astronauts Robert Behnken and Douglas Hurley, along with ESA astronaut Thomas Pesquet and JAXA astronaut Akihiko Hoshide, embarked on a six-month mission to conduct scientific experiments and maintain the ISS. The launch took place from Kennedy Space Center in Florida, using a Falcon 9 rocket and a Crew Dragon spacecraft. The spacecraft successfully docked with the ISS on November 1, 2021, after a two-day journey. During their stay, the astronauts will conduct a variety of experiments in microgravity, including research on human health, materials science, and Earth observation. Wallace remarked, 'I almost but not quite feel bad for him. He's running a dumpster fire of a campaign that continues to get worse by the week.' item.title: Trump's Gas Price Blame-Shifting Sparks Analysts' Criticism
item.description: President Donald Trump has faced criticism from analysts and political observers after attempting to shift blame for high gas prices onto Ukraine's attacks on Russian oil refineries. In a Truth Social post on Monday, October 5, 2026, Trump claimed that Ukraine's actions against Russian refineries, rather than his own policies, were driving up gasoline and diesel prices. He specifically stated that "the word, 'Refineries,' where Russia's are being blown up by Ukraine, and where ours are being closed up, in Blue States, like California, by the Dumocrats (sic)," were responsible for the price surge. The national average for a gallon of regular gas was $4.36 and diesel was $6.23 at the time of his post. Analysts quickly responded to Trump's claims, pointing out the contradictions in his argument. item.description: Senators Bernie Sanders and Ro Khanna are actively campaigning in California to support a proposed 5% one-time tax on the wealth of billionaires in the state, which aims to fund federal Medi-Cal cuts. The initiative, known as Proposition 40, has become a focal point of political contention as early voting begins, with significant financial opposition from billionaire-backed groups. Governor Gavin Newsom, a prominent opponent of the tax, argues that it could lead to billionaires relocating out of California, thereby reducing state revenue. Newsom has proposed a national billionaire tax instead, focusing on loans taken against assets. The opposition to Proposition 40 has raised over $252 million, primarily from tech billionaires like Sergey Brin, John Doerr, and Eric Schmidt. item.title: Palm Beach County GOP Stands by Suspended Clerk Amid Sexual Abuse Allegations
item.description: The Republican Party of Palm Beach County, Florida, has declared its support for Mike Caruso, the suspended Clerk of Courts, despite his August arrest on allegations of sexually abusing a young child. item.title: Air Canada Announces Cancellation of Five Long-Haul International Routes for 2027
item.description: Air Canada has announced the cancellation of five major international long-haul routes for 2027, including flights from Canada to Delhi, Mumbai, Dubai, Singapore, and Algiers. According to a report by Travel Pulse and aviation site Simple Flying, these routes had already been suspended for 2026 and were expected to return in 2027, but the airline has now confirmed they will not resume. The Calgary-Delhi and Toronto-Mumbai routes, previously operated as winter seasonal fifth-freedom services via London Heathrow, will not return. The Toronto-Mumbai service was discontinued in March 2025 due to Russian airspace restrictions following Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Air Canada is also ending its Vancouver-Dubai route, which had not operated since March 2025, and will consolidate Dubai service through Toronto. item.description: A CDC-led study published in the American Journal of Epidemiology on September 10, 2026, reveals that most people with the flu stop isolating when they are still likely contagious, increasing the risk of spreading the virus. The study showed that only 5.5% of people isolate from the community for the full recommended period, and less than 1% isolate from household members for the entire duration. item.description: In a remarkable archaeological discovery, amateur metal detectorist Oliver Riedl unearthed a hoard of 934 Roman silver denarii in Wesseling, Germany, marking the largest collection of its kind from Emperor Hadrian's reign ever found in the country. The coins, buried in a ceramic pot lined with straw, were discovered after Riedl's metal detector continued to beep persistently following the initial find of 15 coins. Authorities from the LVR Office for the Preservation of Archaeological Monuments in the Rhineland were called to the site, where they recovered the entire cache, which now resides at the LVR-LandesMuseum Bonn. The hoard, dating from 148 B.C.E. to 125 C.E., includes coins minted during the reign of Emperor Hadrian (117-138 C.E.), making it the largest such collection from this period in Germany and the fifth-largest globally. item.description: The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is conducting a clinical trial of Gilead Sciences' experimental drug obeldesivir to evaluate its effectiveness in preventing Ebola virus disease following exposure to the Bundibugyo virus. The trial, known as EBO-PEP, is being carried out in Ituri province, where an Ebola outbreak emerged in mid-May 2026. More than 250 individuals are currently participating in the study, with plans to enroll approximately 1,000 adults and children aged 12 and older. Participants must have had contact with someone who tested positive for the Bundibugyo virus within the past five days and must not yet show symptoms. The study is coordinated by the medical humanitarian organization ALIMA, in collaboration with the DRC's National Institute for Biomedical Research and the French organization ANRS. item.title: George Armfield: Victorian Era Dog Painter Celebrated for Detailed Animal Art
item.description: George Armfield (c. 1808–1893) was a British animal painter renowned for his vivid and meticulously detailed portrayals of dogs during the Victorian era. Born George Armfield Smith, he was the son of portrait painter William Armfield Hobday and began exhibiting his work at the Royal Academy at a young age. Specializing in genre scenes featuring terriers, hounds, and other domestic dogs, Armfield captured the energy, character, and everyday behaviors of these animals through broad, expressive brushstrokes. His paintings, which depicted dogs hunting, playing, or resting in rural settings such as barns and fields, were immensely popular with Victorian audiences and remain among the most celebrated examples of 19th-century British animal art. The article highlights several of Armfield's notable works, including 'Dog with Puppies,' 'Gun Dogs in the Long Grass,' 'Spaniel Flushing Pheasant,' 'Three Spaniels and a Flying Mallard,' and 'Two Dogs Resting by Their Master's Lunch Basket.' item.title: US withdraws bombers from RAF Fairford amid security concerns over suspected terror plot
item.description:
The United States Air Force has withdrawn all of its bombers from RAF Fairford, a military air base in Gloucestershire, England, following a suspected terror plot targeting the facility. A Pentagon official confirmed on Sunday that the bombers, which included B-1, B-2, and B-52 aircraft, have been redeployed to their home stations in the United States. The decision comes after British authorities arrested multiple individuals in connection with an alleged terrorist attack planned for the base.
On September 27, five UK nationals in their mid-20s were arrested on suspicion of explosives offenses and terrorism near the military site. They have since been released on bail, along with a sixth suspect, a dual British-Iranian national, who was arrested on October 1 on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts. CEO Andrew Boyd revealed in an exclusive WIRED interview that Paragon cannot see who customers target or the data they extract from devices, relying instead on customer vetting and contractual agreements to prevent abuse. item.description: The WIRED publication has launched an interactive feature that simulates the experience of traveling in the Occupied West Bank. This digital tool provides users with a virtual journey through the region, highlighting the challenges and restrictions faced by travelers in this politically sensitive area. The interactive map and multimedia content aim to educate the public about the complex realities of life under occupation, including checkpoints, restricted movement, and the impact on daily routines. item.title: Glynis Johns' Mermaid Role in 'Miranda' (1948) Featured Unique Rubber Tail Design and Practical Effects
item.description: The article discusses a collection of 20 photographs showcasing Glynis Johns as a mermaid in the 1948 British fantasy comedy film 'Miranda.' Johns portrayed the character Miranda Trewella, a playful and flirtatious mermaid, through specialized practical effects, unique wardrobe designs, and her personal charm. A notable aspect of her transformation was the construction of her mermaid tail, which was designed by The Dunlop Rubber Company. Dunlop created two separate rubber tails for the production: one for swimming scenes that prioritized movement and buoyancy, and another for dry scenes that was designed to be worn with custom gowns. The rubber tail was extremely heavy, immobilizing Johns' legs, requiring crew members and co-stars to physically carry her around the studio lot. item.description: The U.S. military conducted a lethal strike on a vessel in the Caribbean that was suspected of carrying drug traffickers, resulting in the deaths of four individuals on board. The military shared a video showing what appeared to be an explosion destroying the moving vessel. This change aims to encourage large-scale data center development in rural communities, though experts warn that the benefits may not necessarily translate into job creation or local economic growth. The opportunity zone program, initially proposed during the Trump administration, has faced criticism for not effectively driving investment to disadvantaged areas. item.description: Animal welfare organizations are raising concerns about the Utah Department of Agriculture and Food's handling of a bird flu outbreak at a mink farm in Salt Lake County. The outbreak, which has been confirmed in seven captive mink cases as of August, marks the first documented instance of avian influenza in mink in the United States. Advocacy groups, including Animal Wellness Action and the Center for a Humane Economy, have criticized the state's lack of transparency, demanding detailed information on mink-to-mink transmission, worker exposure, and the farm's population. item.title: Security Flaw in ChatGPT's macOS App Allows Potential Data Theft by Attackers
item.description: A recently discovered vulnerability in the macOS version of OpenAI's ChatGPT application has been patched, but it could have allowed attackers to gain access to sensitive user data. The flaw, identified by researchers at the Objective-See Foundation, exploited a trusted component within the app that could be manipulated to deliver untrusted scripts into the main ChatGPT process. This would have enabled attackers to access chat logs, browser sessions, and other stored data, as well as potentially run commands through the application. The vulnerability required an attacker to already have malware installed on a target machine, making it a local exploit. Patrick Wardle, a software analyst at Objective-See, described the flaw as 'insanely trivial' to exploit, requiring only about a dozen lines of code for a proof of concept. item.description:
The Prime Minister of Samoa, Laaulialemalietoa Lea Schmidt, has issued a public apology after a video surfaced showing him performing a Nazi salute and leading a chant of 'Heil Hitler' at a private family gathering in 2007. In the brief seven-second clip, Schmidt can be seen instructing approximately a dozen attendees to raise their right hands in the salute while saying 'Heil Hitler,' with the group complying.
The video was first reported by the Samoa Observer on Sunday, prompting Schmidt to release an official government statement on Monday expressing regret. He acknowledged that regardless of his intentions at the time, the words and actions were inappropriate and could cause offense and pain. Schmidt emphasized that the comments were never meant for public view and stated that the incident does not reflect his personal beliefs or those of the Samoan government.

item.description: The article discusses the growing prominence of Black Twitter on the social media platform Threads, highlighting how it has become a vital hub for Black social media users following the decline of Twitter (now X) under Elon Musk's ownership. Chris Rhodes, 47, the owner of the property, denied being a 'neighbour from hell' despite the severe consequences for his neighbor, Shivarna Mitra, 44. Mitra, who moved into the property in 2021 after recovering from cancer, had invested £80,000 in renovations, intending to make it her 'forever home' with her mother and young son. However, Rhodes began demolishing his half of the house in 2022 without proper planning permission, claiming he was following health and safety guidelines after a storm made the gable wall unsafe. The company announced on October 1 that the program would be paused until the first quarter of 2027, citing a 'significant rise' in automated submissions that were largely invalid or contained hallucinations. item.title: Primordial Magnetic Fields May Resolve Hubble Tension in Cosmic Expansion Measurements
item.description:
Scientists have discovered that tiny magnetic fields generated shortly after the Big Bang could help explain the long-standing discrepancy in measurements of the universe's expansion rate. This 'Hubble tension' arises from two different methods of measuring the Hubble constant, which describes how fast the universe is expanding. One method, based on the cosmic microwave background (CMB) observed by telescopes like Planck, predicts a Hubble constant of approximately 67 kilometers per second per megaparsec (km/s/Mpc). The other method, which measures the brightness of Type Ia supernovae in distant galaxies, yields a higher value of about 73 km/s/Mpc. The difference between these measurements is statistically significant and suggests that our current cosmological model may be incomplete.

He argues that the Supreme Court would likely defer to the political process rather than intervene in a constitutional dispute over Trump's eligibility. Mehlhorn suggests that even if the Court were to rule Trump ineligible, the 'political question' doctrine would prevent them from enforcing such a decision, potentially allowing Trump to assume the presidency through a de facto outcome. The article notes that Trump has repeatedly suggested seeking a third term despite constitutional limitations, and some allies like Steve Bannon have claimed he could circumvent these restrictions. item.title: Oasis take legal action to halt auction of rare unreleased recordings
item.description: Oasis has taken legal action to stop the planned auction of a large archive of previously unheard recordings associated with the band. The collection, known as The Desk Tapes, was assembled by Huw Richards, Oasis’s former front-of-house sound engineer, who worked with the group from 1994 until 2001. It was scheduled to be sold by Littleton Auctions on October 3, with a guide price of £1.2 million to £1.6 million. The archive reportedly included 63 concert recordings, more than 100 hours of rehearsal material, soundchecks, and candid conversations between Noel and Liam Gallagher. Following legal proceedings brought by Oasis, the Gallaghers, and Sony Music Entertainment U.K., the auction house withdrew the lot from the sale. Littleton Auctions’ managing director, Ben Homer, said the recordings had been removed in light of the legal action and expressed disappointment that the archive could not be offered as planned. item.description: Ex-Doctor Who showrunner Russell T. Davies has publicly addressed the detrimental impact of online leaks on the franchise, stating that they have 'more ferocious than ever' and are 'hurting the run' of the show. This widespread leaking has led to fan cynicism, with audiences becoming less surprised by storylines and quicker to assume new ideas would fail. Davies specifically links the decision to cancel the 2026 Christmas Special to the leaks, as the BBC feared public backlash and potential legal action. The BBC was reportedly hesitant to pursue legal action against the leaker, fearing it would appear disproportionate to prosecute a member of the public for copyright infringement. item.description: Brazil's presidential election has set up a rematch between Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who finished first and second in the opening round. item.description: The 1956 Auto Union DKW F93, also known as the 'Big DKW 3=6,' was a notable West German automobile manufactured by Auto Union. This vehicle was powered by a three-cylinder two-stroke engine producing 38 horsepower, which was marketed with the slogan '3=6,' suggesting performance equivalent to a six-cylinder four-stroke engine. The F93 featured a wider body compared to its predecessor, an oval front grille, enhanced suspension, and front-wheel drive. It was available in multiple body styles, including sedan, coupe, and a limited cabriolet version, blending practical design with the unique characteristics of two-stroke engineering. Produced until 1959, the DKW F93 stands as a significant example of postwar German automotive innovation. The car's distinctive style and engineering are captured in the photographs provided, highlighting its role as a unique classic of the 1950s. item.description: A recent incident involving a Trump voter from Ohio, Jack Buhring, who struck and killed a 20-year-old Haitian immigrant named Pierre Damas Bel, has brought attention to the harsh realities of the Trump administration's immigration policies. item.title: Developers submit £16.5 billion data centre plan for former Chapelcross nuclear site in Scotland
item.description:
Developers have submitted planning proposals for a £16.5 billion data centre campus at the former Chapelcross nuclear power station near Annan in Dumfries and Galloway, Scotland. CX Tech Limited is seeking permission to build what it describes as a 'net-zero technology campus' comprising eight data centres with a combined capacity of approximately 1 gigawatt, which would make it one of the largest data centre facilities in the world by power capacity.
The project is expected to create around 750 construction jobs and more than 500 permanent full-time positions once operational. Construction is proposed to begin in 2027, with completion targeted within eight years. The developer states the campus will cover 162,000 square metres and will be powered entirely by locally and regionally generated renewable energy, including wind, solar and biomass sources connected via direct and private-wire arrangements.

item.title: Looney Tunes Film 'Coyote vs. Acme' Surpasses $100 Million at Box Office, Challenges Warner Bros. Decision
item.description: The Looney Tunes comedy 'Coyote vs. Acme,' which was shelved by Warner Bros. as a tax write-off and later rescued by indie distributor Ketchup Entertainment, has grossed over $100 million globally. The film, starring Will Forte and John Cena and produced by DC Studios co-chief James Gunn, was initially deemed financially unworthy by Warner Bros. Discovery CEO David Zaslav, who decided against a theatrical release. Despite a $70 million production cost, the film has earned $59.8 million domestically and $45 million internationally, outperforming other Ketchup-distributed Looney Tunes films like 'The Day the Earth Blew Up,' which grossed only $15.4 million globally. Analysts suggest that Warner Bros. may have missed an opportunity by not investing in stronger marketing, as the film's success was partly driven by positive word of mouth and strong reviews. item.title: Sen. John Kennedy Criticizes Trump for Publicly Sharing Senator Tom Cotton's Cell Number
item.description: Senator John Kennedy (R-La.) has publicly criticized President Donald Trump for sharing the cell phone number of fellow Republican Senator Tom Cotton (R-Ark.) on Truth Social. The incident occurred after Cotton blocked a bill to make daylight saving time permanent, known as the Sunshine Protection Act. Trump posted Cotton's number on his Truth Social account, urging supporters to call him to 'let him know' about the House-passed bill. Kennedy, speaking on NBC's 'Meet the Press,' referred to Trump as his 'friend' but expressed disapproval of the president's decision to publicly disclose Cotton's personal contact information. Kennedy stated, 'I don't think he should have given out Tom's cell phone number. I don't think that's going to help convince Tom,' adding that Trump 'exists loudly' and can be 'tempestuous,' noting he 'can go from zero to a-hole in about three seconds.' item.title: US Marine Arrested in Okinawa for Alleged Murder and Burglary of 39-Year-Old Woman
item.description: A U.S. Marine was arrested in Okinawa, Japan, on suspicion of burglary and murder, sparking widespread outrage both in Japan and internationally. According to The Associated Press, the 29-year-old service member was taken into custody for allegedly killing a 39-year-old woman in a hotel in Naha, the capital of Okinawa, and stealing her wallet and belongings afterward. Police footage reportedly showed the Marine entering the hotel with the victim and leaving alone. The incident has caused significant tension between the U.S. and Japan, with Okinawa Governor Genta Koja stating that the case "deals a major shock and adds fear to the Okinawans who have already been forced to live next to U.S. bases." Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi condemned the incident in a statement to CNN, calling it "an extremely brutal and heinous incident" and expressing "profound regret," while also noting that the Japanese government has lodged a strong protest with the U.S. side. item.description: Aaron Sorkin, the acclaimed screenwriter and director, has shared his thoughts on Jesse Eisenberg's decision to decline the role of Mark Zuckerberg in his upcoming film 'The Social Reckoning,' which serves as a follow-up to his 2010 film 'The Social Network.' However, Eisenberg ultimately declined, stating he was moving in different directions in his life and didn't want to be associated with the character. item.description: The Baltimore Ravens secured a 24-7 halftime lead over the Tennessee Titans before halftime, with quarterback Lamar Jackson suffering an ankle injury in the first half. Despite initial concerns, Jackson was not ruled out for the remainder of the game and was seen smiling on the sideline, indicating the injury was not as severe as feared. Head coach Jesse Minter confirmed Jackson was dealing with 'a little bit of an ankle' and that the team was not overly concerned. The Ravens chose to hold back Jackson for the second half, relying on backup quarterback Tyler Huntley to close out the game. This decision was based on the Ravens' confidence in their lead and the Titans' poor performance, as the Titans entered the game with a 0-4 record and the third-worst scoring average in the NFL at 12.3 points per game. item.title: Attorney Says Cornell Student Alleging Sexual Assault Has Received Threats
item.description:
A former Cornell University student who alleges that she was sexually assaulted by seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity is facing threats intended to pressure her to withdraw a civil lawsuit, according to her attorney, Thomas Giuffra. The woman, identified in court documents as Jane Doe, alleges that the assault occurred overnight on October 19–20, 2024, while she was under the influence of ketamine, alcohol, and marijuana.
Giuffra said that individuals attempting to identify Jane Doe have also targeted at least three women who were mistakenly identified as the accuser. He said both his client and other women have received threats, and he reported that he himself had been threatened. Giuffra did not identify those responsible or say whether the threats had been reported to law enforcement.

item.description: A truck driver who voted for Donald Trump for the first time in 2024 is grappling with guilt after his vehicle struck and killed a 20-year-old Haitian immigrant named Pierre Damas Bel near Springfield, Ohio, on August 31, 2026. Bel, who had Temporary Protected Status (TPS) due to instability in Haiti, lost his legal status when the Supreme Court allowed the Trump administration to end TPS for Haitians. Buhring described the moment of impact, stating he felt a 'big thump' and could feel the collision. He also mentioned making eye contact with Bel before the accident. item.description: Brazilians participated in a pivotal presidential election on Sunday, October 4, 2026, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva facing off against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former President Jair Bolsonaro. item.title: Vietnamese NASA Scientist Advances Miniaturization of Atomic Clocks for Deep Space Missions
item.description: Vietnamese-born scientist Hoang Thai, a principal investigator at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in California, is leading research to develop ultra-precise atomic clocks that can withstand the extreme conditions of deep space. The team's work focuses on miniaturizing quantum sensors, which use atomic properties and quantum phenomena to measure time, gravity, electromagnetic fields, and other physical variables with exceptional accuracy. Current quantum setups are typically confined to laboratories due to their reliance on delicate lasers, vacuum chambers, magnetic shielding, and strictly controlled environments. Thai's team aims to overcome the 'SWaP' challenge—optimizing size, weight, and power consumption—to create compact, rugged clocks suitable for spacecraft. One of their projects involves scaling down a microwave clock to the size of a one-liter container, with potential applications for future GPS satellites. item.description: President Donald Trump's administration has come under fire for its handling of government-funded political advertisements, particularly after CNN anchor Jake Tapper flagged a political ad supporting Trump that aired during an NFL game. The game focuses on cleaning and redecorating a castle room by room, requiring players to put items in their rightful places, remove dirt and rubbish, and repair banners and rugs. item.description: The final online post of Simon Andriesz, a British banker who exposed Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's business connections to Jeffrey Epstein, has resurfaced, sparking renewed concern over his recent death. item.description: The article discusses the rarity of rockets achieving more than 20 launches per year, with SpaceX's Falcon 9 being the only rocket to exceed 50 launches from a single launch pad. It highlights that only China and SpaceX currently have over 50 launches annually, with China employing a Russian-style approach using multiple launch pads and expendable rockets. The piece details SpaceX's journey to achieving high launch reliability, noting that the Falcon 9 reached approximately 90% reliability through 2016, following incidents like the CRS-7 loss in 2015 and the AMOS-6 pad loss in 2016. After returning to flight in January 2017, the Falcon 9 operated without failure until Block 5 entered service in May 2018. By 2019-2020, the cumulative success rate had reached 95%, with the statistical lower bound approaching 98%. item.title: Oil Prices and Inflation Expectations Drive Global Bond-Market Turmoil as Debt Risks Persist
item.description:
Global bond markets are facing renewed turmoil as investors reassess the outlook for inflation, interest rates, and government borrowing. Soaring oil prices have emerged as a clear catalyst for the recent rise in bond yields, because more expensive energy can push consumer prices higher and make it more difficult for central banks to reduce interest rates. Higher expected inflation generally lowers the appeal of existing bonds, whose fixed payments become less valuable in real terms, leading investors to demand higher yields.
Government debt levels are also drawing increased attention. Many countries have accumulated substantial debt, limiting their fiscal flexibility and raising concerns about how governments will finance future deficits. If investors become less confident in a government’s ability to manage its debt burden, they may demand additional compensation for holding that country’s bonds. item.description:
Kerala's Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala has ordered a Vigilance investigation into allegations of irregularities during the tenure of current Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar as the state's Public Works Department (PWD) Secretary. item.title: Meta Claims Billions in Tax Credits by Classifying AI Data Centers as Experimental
item.description:
Meta is using an aggressive tax strategy to claim billions of dollars in research and experimentation tax credits by classifying its AI data centers as experimental pilot models, according to people familiar with the company's operations. The approach allows Meta to receive taxpayer subsidies for expensive computer chips from companies like Nvidia, even though these components are commercially proven technology widely used across the industry.
The tax break, created during the Reagan administration in the 1980s, was designed to encourage American companies to take risks on uncertain technological innovations. Companies must meet a complex four-part test proving they are conducting genuine experiments rather than standard business operations. While thousands of companies benefit from this credit, they typically claim it for researcher and engineer salaries, not for physical infrastructure and equipment.

By age five, he was already performing with his parents, Joe and Myra Keaton, in a physically demanding act where his father would throw him around the stage, drop him down stairs, and hurl him into the audience or through windows. To ensure safety, Buster had a hidden suitcase handle sewn into his costumes for precise handling. The company plans to launch its SR75 suborbital vehicle in spring 2027, depending on the completion of remaining operational requirements and favorable weather conditions. The SR75 is a lightweight, aerodynamically stabilized suborbital rocket intended for research and technology demonstration missions, including applications related to microgravity and hypersonic flight. It is not designed to deploy satellites. The license followed a regulatory review of HyImpulse’s systems and safety procedures. item.description: The article discusses how Donald Trump's military actions and policies have inadvertently accelerated the global transition to renewable energy sources. The author, Thom Hartmann, argues that Trump's decision to engage in a conflict that has driven up oil prices has led to a significant reduction in global oil demand, with the International Energy Agency reporting a 2.5% annual decrease in oil consumption, equivalent to removing 42 million gas-powered vehicles from roads. item.title: Oregon Man Trapped by Boulder Uses Earbuds to Call for Rescue
item.description:
Joseph Little, a 28-year-old Oregon resident, was rescued after a large boulder pinned him against rocks near the Marina in Warrenton, Oregon. The incident occurred early on September 26 while Little was on an uneven section of jetty extending into the Columbia River, approximately 90 miles northwest of Portland.
According to Sgt. Dylan McCoy of the Warrenton Police Department, the boulder became dislodged and fell onto Little, trapping his upper body and legs. Although authorities did not know the rock’s exact weight, McCoy estimated that it weighed about a ton. The boulder landed near an area where high tide regularly pushes water over the rocks, creating a serious risk that Little could drown if help did not arrive quickly.

item.title: Brazilian Bellbirds and Seriemas Among the Loudest Birds Ever Recorded
item.description:
A new scientific study has identified some of the loudest birds ever documented, with vocalizations that surpass the noise of jackhammers, chainsaws, and even elephant trumpets. The research, led by evolutionary biologist João Mes and published in the journal Evolution, focused on two Brazilian species: the bare-throated bellbird and the red-legged seriema.
Despite being only about the size of a dove, the bare-throated bellbird produces sharp, metallic calls from the canopy of Brazil's Serra do Mar mountains that can overwhelm listeners. These calls, used primarily to attract mates, rank among the most deafening sounds ever recorded in the avian world. The red-legged seriema matches this volume, joining a previously recognized bellbird species as one of the loudest birds known to science.
The researchers also discovered several anatomical features that enable these birds to produce such powerful songs, offering new insights into the mechanics of avian vocalizations. The findings chal

item.title: Alert, the World's Northernmost Inhabited Place
item.description: Alert, located on Ellesmere Island in Nunavut, Canada, is recognized as the northernmost permanently inhabited settlement on Earth. Situated at approximately 82°30'N latitude, this remote outpost serves as a critical research station for environmental and climate studies. The community, established in 1950 as a military base, now supports a small population of scientists and support staff who conduct year-round research on Arctic ecosystems, atmospheric conditions, and climate change. Despite its extreme location, Alert has basic amenities including a small store, a post office, and a medical facility. The area experiences six months of continuous daylight in summer and six months of darkness in winter, creating unique challenges for residents. The settlement's isolation and harsh climate make it a vital location for understanding the impacts of global warming on polar regions. item.title: Trump Administration Forms UFO Advisory Panel to Review Unidentified Aerial Phenomena
item.description: The New York Times reports that President Donald Trump’s administration has created a new advisory council focused on unidentified anomalous phenomena, commonly known as UAPs or UFOs. The panel, formed during the administration’s release of government records on the subject, includes scientists who are open to the possibility that some sightings could involve extraterrestrial technology. Harvard astrophysicist Avi Loeb chairs the group and has argued that even a single confirmed case of alien technological origin would represent an extraordinary scientific discovery. The administration has released files that include previously surfaced military footage, reports, and government material discussing topics such as interstellar wormholes. Trump said the records were being made public so people could assess the information themselves. item.title: Brewers Secure NLDS Game 1 Victory Following Controversial Home Run Call at American Family Field
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers defeated the San Diego Padres 3-2 in Game 1 of the National League Division Series (NLDS) at American Family Field, securing a crucial victory in the best-of-five playoff series. The game featured a dramatic and controversial moment in the seventh inning when Brewers catcher William Contreras hit a solo home run off Padres pitcher Adrian Morejon, which proved to be the decisive run. Contreras' home run, his second hit against San Diego pitching this season, came after a tense sequence where the Brewers had loaded the bases with two outs. The game remained tied until Contreras' hit, which gave Milwaukee a 3-2 lead. The Padres had a chance to tie the game in the ninth inning when first baseman Ty France appeared to hit a go-ahead two-run home run, but the ball struck a truss in the stadium's roof and bounced down, where it was caught by Brewers outfielder Jackson Chourio. item.title: Republicans Struggle to Find an Effective Campaign Target for the 2026 Midterms
item.description: Republicans are struggling to identify a single, consistently effective Democratic target for the 2026 midterm elections, according to a POLITICO review of campaign advertising in competitive House and Senate races. In past cycles, figures such as Joe Biden and Nancy Pelosi served as powerful symbols that Republican candidates could use to energize conservative voters and frame Democrats as out of touch. This year, however, those familiar targets have lost some of their political usefulness. Biden remains the Democrat most frequently mentioned in Republican advertisements, appearing across dozens of races, but his lower public profile since leaving office has made him a less potent foil than he was during the 2024 campaign. At a comparable point in that cycle, Biden had been referenced in more than 1,000 Republican House and Senate ads, according to AdImpact data cited by POLITICO.
